facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary finds the key fits the lock of the hidden garden door, turns it, and enters the secret garden.
facts.quote: she put the key in and turned it. It took two hands to do it, but it did turn.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: secret garden
facts.quote: She was standing _inside_ the secret garden.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary is beginning to skip with a skipping-rope, improving with practice.
facts.quote: You can’t skip a hundred at first, but if you practice you’ll mount up.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary skips round the gardens and up and down walks with the rope Martha gave her.
facts.quote: She skipped round the fountain garden, and up one walk and down another.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Martha gives Mary a skipping-rope bought with her mother's money.
facts.quote: I’ve brought thee a present.

facts.subject: Martha Sowerby
facts.value: Martha skips in the middle of the room to show Mary how a skipping-rope is used.
facts.quote: And she ran into the middle of the room and, taking a handle in each hand, began to skip

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary's wish to see the garden and the key she found => she resolves to carry the key with her so she is ready to find the hidden door.
facts.quote: she made up her mind that she would always carry it with her when she went out, so that if she ever should find the hidden door she would be ready.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Fresh moor air and exercise => Mary's mind and imagination are awakening and she cares more about things.
facts.quote: There is no doubt that the fresh, strong, pure air from the moor had a great deal to do with it.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: The robin seems to lead Mary; she wonders whether it knows where the door is.
facts.quote: You ought to show me the door today; but I don’t believe you know!

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: friend
facts.quote: You do cheer me up,” she said. “I like to hear you talk.”

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary tells the robin she is the first person to speak in the garden for ten years.
facts.quote: I am the first person who has spoken in here for ten years.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: the walled garden
facts.quote: She walked under one of the fairy-like gray arches between the trees and looked up at the sprays and tendrils which formed them.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary digs and weeds around the pale green shoots in the old flowerbeds of the garden.
facts.quote: she thought she would skip round the whole garden

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary searches for a sharp piece of wood and digs and weeds around the pale green shoots.
facts.quote: She searched about until she found a rather sharp piece of wood and knelt down and dug and weeded out the weeds and grass

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary could not spell particularly well.
facts.quote: She could not spell particularly well but she found that she could print letters when she tried.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary can print letters when she tries.
facts.quote: she found that she could print letters when she tried.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary says she knows how to write.
facts.quote: "I know how to write," Mary answered.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary is given a shilling a week to spend, paid every Saturday.
facts.quote: Mrs. Medlock said I was to have a shilling a week to spend.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary dictates a printed letter to Dickon asking him to buy flower seeds and garden tools at Thwaite.
facts.quote: Then it was a serious piece of work to write to Dickon.

facts.subject: Dickon Sowerby
facts.value: Dickon can make flowers grow, according to Martha.
facts.quote: Our Dickon can make a flower grow out of a brick walk.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mr. Craven discovers the open door => he would get a new key and lock the garden forever
facts.quote: if Mr. Craven found out about the open door he would be fearfully angry and get a new key and lock it up forevermore

facts.subject: world
facts.value: Mary hears far-off crying in the corridors again, a sound with no clear source that has now been heard three times.
facts.quote: And I heard that far-off crying again, just as we heard it the other night.

facts.subject: Mary Lennox
facts.value: Mary falls asleep in an armchair after her morning of digging and the afternoon's excitement.
facts.quote: so comfortably tired that she fell asleep.
